page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.4xlarge is a dedicated compute-oriented virtual machine instance belonging to the High Clock Speed ecs.hfc5 family. Built on the KVM hypervisor and the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 6149 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. The configuration allocates 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores using hyperthreading, backed by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 22 MB L3 cache. Vector extensions include AVX and AVX-512F alongside cryptographic AES acceleration.

The hardware configuration provides 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached cloud storage for non-volatile file persistence. Networking capabilities feature a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and no discrete GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent middle-tier multi-threaded execution set against lower single-core throughput. While single-thread benchmarks such as Geekbench single-core (1095.0), stress-ng single-core (1356.18), and gzip compression (23.29 GB/sec) rank in the bottom 25%, multi-core metrics sit squarely in the middle 50%. Notable results include a PassMark CPU score of 15463.52, Geekbench multi-core score of 6654.0, and Clang compilation test score of 12381.0. Memory throughput reaches 73.32 GB/sec for uncached reads and 38.81 GB/sec for writes.

With its 2.0 GB per vCPU memory density and 16 compute threads, the instance delivers balanced cost efficiency for scale-out parallel tasks rather than single-threaded bottlenecks. It handles data pipelines and web workloads adequately, achieving 13.86 million Redis SET operations per second and 7.98 GB/sec static web serving throughput. It is best suited for CI/CD compilation, multi-threaded batch processing, application backends, and distributed caching tiers.
